streams.status_detail: PR #34 has been merged into main (merge commit 50a54227444ae52bdb5641b30e8c430ec7b8a722). Exact-head quality CI 45797079222 passed all steps. The new evidence is from Lloyd's Register Foundation's World Risk Poll 2025 / From alert to agency report (published 2026-10-13): 143,459 respondents in 140 countries; 80% of disaster-impacted respondents reported an advance warning, and 64% of warned respondents said they could act. Action rose from 37% with one warning channel to 51% with two and 64% with three; these are associations, not causal effects. Crucially, Georgia had only 99 respondents asked about warning channels (101 impacted); the 22.8% figure appears only under an alternative >=100 impacted threshold, and Georgia is excluded by the report's >=100 asked threshold. The source repository reports Python/R reproduction of 541 findings (487 exact match, 17 within tolerance, 37 Gallup-only); NOEMA has not independently rerun the microdata. The merged evidence record and privacy-preserving Action Readiness Ledger proposal contain no survey microdata or personal data. No Georgian municipal dataset or field validation exists.
streams.next_step: Select one Georgian river-basin/municipal workflow only after obtaining the current official data dictionary and explicit permission for aggregated alert-delivery, acknowledgement and action-completion records. Design a preregistered baseline and pilot evaluation; do not treat the small Georgia WRP sample as an operational estimate or duplicate official alerting.
